[{"text":"Oracle-bone and bronze examples document 日 in early inscriptional traditions. The sources report oracle-bone uses for the sun, daylight, and a day unit, but do not verify the dates of the individual inscriptions. The documented script categories include oracle-bone, bronze, manuscript, and seal forms; the evidence does not date every form or establish a detailed sequence of graphic changes.","evidence_ids":["ref014","ref015","ref020","ref028","ref043","ref049"]},{"text":"The received Han-era Shuowen account analyzes 日 as 从囗一, interpreting the outline as the sun and the inner stroke as its undiminished center. This is a later explanation, not direct evidence for the graph's earliest structure.","evidence_ids":["ref003","ref016","ref021"]}]

Modern readings and dictionary glosses alone do not establish a chronology or semantic path for later uses. Present-day Chinese dictionaries also record 日 as an abbreviation for Japan, but the evidence does not date its origin.
